newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Several injured at Cambodian garment protest.
newsitem.headline: Several injured at Cambodian garment protest.

text.p: Labour unrest at a Cambodian garment factory erupted into violence on Thursday as police threw punches at opposition leader Sam Rainsy and his deputy and fired shots into the air, witnesses said.
At least seven workers were injured in the fracas, but none seriously, witnesses said.

Witnesses said Khieu Rada, secretary general of Sam Rainsy's unrecognised Khmer Nation Party (KNP), was punched repeatedly until he bled from the mouth, and several workers were hit, but Sam Rainsy, who was protected by five bodyguards, was uninjured.
Rainsy said he planned to return to the factory later in the day to lure workers outside for another demonstration.

Pen Kimsieng, a factory supervisor at the Hong Kong-owned Tack Fat Garments Ltd, said she saw at least six workers being hit by police, who were trying to break up the demonstration. One was bleeding from the head, she said.
"I am very surprised by the reaction of the police. This shows the police are serving the interests of the investors," Sam Rainsy told reporters later.
The incident was the fourth protest at the Tack Fat factory and the ninth since December 10, when Sam Rainsy formed a union for garment workers.
In the past week, the government has become increasingly forceful in shutting down the strikes, all of which have been led by Sam Rainsy, as industry officials complain of cancelled orders.
On Saturday, police used fire houses to break up a demonstration. On Wednesday, they pushed Sam Rainsy off the Tack Fat factory grounds in shutting down another demonstration.

Cambodian garment industry workers have complained of low pay, long hours and poor conditions. Analysts have attributed the worsening labour unrest to the growing pains of one of Cambodia's fastest-growing industries.
Tack Fat representatives said they reached a settlement with workers five days ago, including better pay and benefits, and hundreds of workers reported to the factory for work on Thursday.
But Sam Rainsy, who said the settlement was reached without enough worker representation, broke through a police roadblock to encourage a few dozen workers to strike.
At the factory gates, about 10 to 15 police lunged toward him, throwing punches at him and his five bodyguards, witnesses said.
Police fired several times into the air with automatic weapons as Sam Rainsy and his bodyguards were pushed into the street and jumped into their car, witnesses said.
Speaking with a mouthful of blood, Khieu Rada said he was beaten by police as he tried to hail a motorbike taxi.
Chief of Penal Police Mok Chito, who pushed Sam Rainsy off of factory property on Wednesday, said police had shot into the air to protect themselves in the confusion.
